added.summary: Scene changes with their assets fetched first: og.scene.preload loads a scene (a GameDesc.scenes name or an asset id) and asks for every streaming group it declares, og.scene.progress answers how much of them has arrived (bytes, received, fraction, ready, the groups still waiting), og.scene.change puts it in place as the next tick starts (the scene before it despawned with its descendants, what the game spawned kept) and sends og.SceneChanged, and og.scene.current names the scene in place. A change asked for is og.SceneState, world state: a save taken between the call and the tick carries it. A world that never changes scene registers nothing.

The loading screen as one API on every host: project.ogt `publish { loading engine | game | page }` (written by og build) says who draws it, og.loading.stage reports a stage with a fraction and a label, og.loading.idle says the renderer has nothing left to compile or upload, og.loading.done ends it once, and og.loading.status reads it back. With `game` the engine's splash covers only its own boot and the game's first frames are its loading screen; with `page` the canvas stays hidden and the page draws its own loader.

A published page sends og:progress, og:stage, og:first-frame, og:loaded, og:ready and og:failed as window events, and, when framed, as postMessage({ source: "origin-engine", type, detail }) to the parent, so any page hosting the game can draw its own loader without the platform (docs/web-export.md §Loading events). `publish { loading_labels { fetch "…" } }` renames the splash's stages.

The bytes of a group's pack received so far (its size once resident), with StreamStatus.progress, the fraction: a pending group's download is readable for a loading bar, on the web as the fetch streams in.
How much of a pending bundle (og.load.bundle) the host has received: bytes received, total when known, and the fraction.

While a segment plays, the first chunk of every segment a choice may cut to (and of the next segment) is read ahead, on one deck as on two, so a cut to any option starts without waiting for its video.
